note: The reference contract for Tier B. Firmware-derived images and everything captured from them stay local: the reference root is inside out/, which is gitignored (.gitignore line 9) and never committed. This file is the contract, not the images.

rules: Tokens are lowercase ASCII from the matrix tables below; ids may contain '-' but never '__'.
One file is one cell: a reference never covers more than one state/theme/background/resolution combination.
Frames are stored at the cell's own resolution (1920x1080 or 1280x720). Never rescale a reference to make it pair.
A reference without its <name>.state.json provenance file is still paired, but the scorecard marks the cell 'provenance missing' and refuses to call it a pass.

fields.cell: the cell id, exactly the file's basename without .png
fields.captured: ISO date the frame was taken from the emulator
fields.firmware: the vsh.self firmware version the frame came from (4.93)
fields.rpcs3Build: the RPCS3 build/commit used, or 'unknown' for a pre-contract frame
fields.preset: the console preset and the RPCS3 renderer settings that affect the picture (Vulkan, 1920x1080, exclusive fullscreen disabled)
fields.clock: the console/PCRTC values the frame was taken at, if known; 'unknown' otherwise
fields.sha256: sha256 of the PNG bytes, so a moved or replaced file is detectable
fields.note: anything a reader must know before treating the number as fidelity

pairing.rule: A captured cell pairs with the reference whose basename equals the cell id. A cell with no reference is reported as 'no reference yet', never scored against a different state.
pairing.dimensionRule: If the reference and the capture differ in size, the cell is reported as 'dimension mismatch' and not scored; nothing is rescaled.
pairing.registered: A few references predate this contract. They are listed under 'registered' with their real path and are paired by the cell id there; everything else is discovered by scanning the reference root.
pairing.refreshing: A reference is replaced deliberately (a matched state, a corrected renderer, a new firmware capture) and the change is recorded in native-xmb/audit/PARITY-SCORECARD.md with a dated reason. A reference is never updated to make a failing screen pass.

notReferences: out/native-reference/layers/*.png are deterministic native self-baselines used by work/ab-layers.ts. They prove repeatability and catch drawing changes; they are not firmware references and must never be scored as Tier B.
native-xmb/screenshots/* and docs/screenshots/* are documentation images.

matrix.note: States come from work/parity-catalogue.json. The theme axis is the three states appearance/background and appearance/theme actually produce in this build; the plan's 'Original + the four presets' background presets are the background axis, because one pinned background clock selects both the ICONS.mnu override (icons.cpp:50-65) and the LINE1/PARTICLES preset (ribbon.cpp:341-345) - capturing them as two axes would count the same pin twice. That is stated in PARITY-SCORECARD.md.

themes.note: appearance/background 0: the wave, particles and the reconstructed icon material (the canonical capture's theme)
appearance/background 1: the firmware 'classic' background path; native particles are hidden
the firmware's own theme (stored in dev_flash, not user content) through the p3t path: theme background image, icontable, sound roles

backgrounds.note: the traced daylight pin, at the DATE the matched day references were captured (2026-10-28): the month phase is (day-1)/daysInMonth*30, so 10-28 gives 26.129 while 10-25 gives 23.2258, and the canonical gate removed that 3.7/255 depression by matching the date. 10:00 is 3/4 of the way from the 07:00 yoake key to the 11:00 day key (icons.cpp:64-65), so this cell is daylight as the reference frame saw it, not the exact preset key
night is held from 23:00 to 01:00, so midnight is the preset's own value
yoake is reached at 05:00 and held to 07:00
higure is reached at 17:00 and held to 19:00

resolutions.note: fullscreen at the monitor's own 1920x1080 (the canonical capture)
a windowed 1280x720 framebuffer: the host has no 720p display mode, so the console's own 720p projection is P10's work, not this cell's

matrix.size: 25 capturable states x 3 themes x 4 backgrounds x 2 resolutions = 600 cells; one cell is one capture

rpcs3.howTo: native-xmb/HANDOFF-PHASES.md, section 'Capturing the real XMB in RPCS3 (how-to, learned 2026-10-25)' (lines 102-121)
rpcs3.boot: rpcs3.exe --no-gui --config <scratch yml> <dev_flash>/vsh/module/vsh.self, with the scratch config outside the repo and outside the RPCS3 folder; never close an RPCS3 the user started
rpcs3.renderer: Vulkan, 1920x1080; 'Exclusive Fullscreen Mode: Disable' (with exclusive fullscreen, desktop capture returns one frozen frame while the overlay still reports 60 FPS)
rpcs3.captureMethod: desktop CopyFromScreen of the whole 1920x1080 frame after the scripted navigation settles; PrintWindow returns stale frames under Vulkan
rpcs3.input: vsh.self ignores --input-config, so RPCS3 uses config/input_configs/global/Default.yml. Back it up, check its sha256 before and after (the user's original is e624da0d66a8e971173c39a69a1dc2c89ffe146d57bf2a03c2c8cfacb459ceee), map Cross/Circle to PgDown/PgUp, and restore the file in the same run. Changing it needs the user's approval every time.
perCellRecipe: 1. Boot with the scratch config and wait for the settled XMB (the 'Preloading cached shaders' overlay must be gone; if it stalls over a minute, restart).

2. Drive the state with the keyboard map: arrows for column/row moves, PgDown for Cross (open), PgUp for Circle (back), Backspace for the PS button. The route in work/parity-catalogue.json is the same route the native capture runs, translated key for key.

3. Match the cell's pinned state before grabbing: theme (console Theme Settings), background preset (console Date and Time, or the equivalent clock), output resolution, and the console's own clock string.
4. Let the transition settle (the page move is about 300 ms; two seconds is enough), then CopyFromScreen the full frame.
5. Save as <root>/<state>__<theme>__<background>__<resolution>.png and write the provenance sidecar described above.
6. Record in the scorecard why the frame is matched or not (console clock, profile, content set) - the one number that matters is whether the state is matched, not how high the score is.
rpcs3.notRunHere: This tool never launches RPCS3. The rig belongs to the capture agent (PARITY-PHASES dispatch row for P0.3); work/parity.ts only reads the reference set and reports what is missing.
rpcs3.matrixRecipe: Run the cell list printed by 'bun work/parity.ts --matrix' in firmware order: one console session per state, walking the four background presets (day, night, yoake, higure) and both resolutions, and switching the theme once per state (original, classic, 01.p3t). A cell that cannot be produced on the console (no PSN, no disc, a menu the firmware will not show without content) is recorded as 'unavailable' in the scorecard rather than captured from a different state.

retired.replacedBy: the matched day-window capture imported from C:/dev/out/rpcs3-day-2026-10-28 (console clock 10/28 10:00 AM, MM/DD, 12-Hour, theme Original evidenced in the same session)
retired.note: The pre-contract RPCS3 frame work/ab-layers.ts scores against (2026-10-25, 4.93, DD/MM 24-hour console clock). It stayed registered until a matched root capture existed; that capture now does, so the registered entry is retired rather than kept as a permanent mismatch-by-construction. work/ab-layers.ts still uses this PNG for its own historical comparison - that is a different instrument and is untouched.

budgets.revisionNote: First policy. Every number below is a target, not a measurement: no matched RPCS3 reference exists yet, so the only measured firmware comparison in the tree is the unmatched root pair (18.20 dB / 0.8388 whole frame, work/ab-layers.thresholds.json). The budgets are set where a matched state could plausibly land, so the first matched reference produces an honest pass or an honest fail; they are not set at today's values minus a delta, which is the regression-gate pattern in work/ab-layers.thresholds.json and would prove nothing about firmware fidelity.
budgets.datedChangeRule: A budget changes only with a dated entry here (updated + revisionNote) and a matching dated paragraph in native-xmb/audit/PARITY-SCORECARD.md. Widening a budget to make a failing screen pass is not a change; it is the failure being hidden.

icon-heavy.rationale: Root and the ten columns: the structure is icons, labels and the clock over the wave. The unmatched root pair measures 18.20 dB / 0.8388, and its whole-frame error is dominated by content that differs by construction. A matched column should clear 20 dB / 0.90 on the frame and on each required region; the category icon row is the tightest structural region, and the item label row carries the glyph phase, so it fails first when text placement is wrong.

text-heavy.rationale: List and form pages (settings submenus, folder pages, the download page, the Jellyfin sign-in page, Continue Watching). Text-dominated regions score lower than structure even on a matched state because the console's glyph phase and coverage compositing are not reproduced bit-exactly (audit/TEXT-RASTER.md); the glyph-metric half of this class's policy is still open (P3.1) and the crop gate is the interim budget.

composite.rationale: Transient and overlay surfaces (options panel, dialog, notification, volume HUD, PS menu, OSK, player panel). The surface region is what matters, not the scene under it; a region may raise its own budget where the console is unambiguous (the PS menu blacks the frame, so its entries are gated at 26 dB / 0.95).

budgets.regionOverrides: A region in work/parity-catalogue.json may carry psnrDb/ssim to tighten or relax its class budget. Tightening is always allowed; relaxing is a dated change.
